subject: tabs
title: Angular tabs cannot render rich tab labels; React and Vue can
description: React TabItem.label is a ReactNode and Vue offers a tab:<value> slot used both in the tab and in the overflow menu. Angular hw-tab only has a required string label input that is interpolated as text, so icons, counters or badges in tab labels are impossible in Angular.

evidence.quote: export interface TabItem { value: string; label: ReactNode; content: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean }

expected: Equivalent label projection in Angular (e.g. an optional <ng-template hwTabLabel> inside hw-tab, used for the tab and the overflow item), as React/Vue provide.
fix: Add a label template query to HwTabComponent and render it with ngTemplateOutlet in both the tab button and the overflow item, keeping label as the text fallback and accessible name.
repro: Code reading of the three adapters.
verifierNote: Read packages/angular/src/navigation.ts:7-20 (HwTabComponent and hw-tabs template) and the built packages/angular/dist/fesm2022 template; React interactive.tsx:9, :82, :86; Vue interactive.ts:66 and README.md:83; Angular README.md:79; searched all adapters for a tab-label template/directive (none). Angular HwTabComponent has only `@Input({required: true}) label = '';` (navigation.ts:10), interpolated as `{{ tab.label }}` in both the tab button and the overflow item (also present twice in the built dist). No ng-template/ContentChild for labels exists in packages/angular/src. React `TabItem.label: ReactNode` (interactive.tsx:9) renders `{item.label}` in the tab (:82) and overflow item (:86); Vue renders `slots[`tab:${item.value}`]?.({ item }) ?? item.label` (interactive.ts:66) and documents `optional tab:value label slots` (README.md:83); vanilla tabs are author markup. Angular therefore cannot render icons/badges/counters in tab labels.

subject: breadcrumb

description: When the last item has an href, React and Vue output <a href aria-current="page">, so the current page stays a focusable, clickable link. Angular never links the last item, and the documented mapping says the current page is text. The DGA checklist row quoted in the repo requires the current page to be disabled and non-interactive.

subject: stepper
title: Completed and upcoming step states have no text equivalent
description: Only the current step is exposed (aria-current="step"). Complete vs upcoming is conveyed only by the CSS check-mark mask and colour; no adapter renders visually hidden state text, and the API offers no prop for it. The accessibility tree of the framework examples reads "Details / Review / Complete" with no completion state, while the vanilla guide example works around it by authoring "Details — complete" into the label. Explicit status overrides (e.g. a completed later step) are therefore invisible to screen readers.

evidence.quote:
return
  • {item.label}
Present current progress, previous/next context, and a text equivalent

expected: WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships: state conveyed visually must be programmatically determinable; docs/dga-reference.md:77 asks for a text equivalent of progress.
fix: Render a visually hidden state suffix per step (localisable completeLabel/upcomingLabel props, Arabic and English defaults resolved from lang) in every adapter and the vanilla controller.
repro: <scratch>/audit/work/nav-a/nav-test.cjs -> stepper: "complete:\"DetailsPersonal data\" | current(step):\"Review\" | upcoming:\"Send\"" in all adapters (no state text); stepMarkers: complete ::before content "" with mask. Evidence aria trees: evidence/components/stepper/react.en.aria.yml lists "listitem: Details" (no state) vs vanilla.en.aria.yml "listitem: Details — complete".
verifierNote: Ran <scratch>/audit/verify/nav-a/bc-stepper.cjs (guide editor, en/ltr light, same breadcrumb and stepper data in React, Vue and Angular; output <scratch>/audit/verify/nav-a/bc-stepper.out). Read React display.tsx:207-218, Vue display.ts:208-213, Angular navigation.ts:194-207, vanilla packages/vanilla/src/stepper.ts:26-39, styles components.css:265-269, docs/dga-reference.md:77, docs/stepper-states.md:123-125. Aria snapshots in all three frameworks: `list "Progress": listitem (Details/Personal data), listitem: Review, listitem: Send` and for an explicit override `list "Override": listitem: Alpha, listitem: Beta, listitem: Gamma` although Gamma is drawn with the completed check mark (markers line: `complete:"\"\""` i.e. ::before content is empty and the number is replaced by the CSS mask tick, components.css:269). Only the current step is exposed (aria-current=step). No adapter or the vanilla controller (stepper.ts:35-38 only sets data-state/aria-current) emits state text, and no prop exists for it; Only React can work around it, because StepItem.label is a ReactNode (display.tsx:207); Vue (display.ts:208 label: string) and Angular (navigation.ts:194 label: string) labels are text only. In a purely linear stepper completion is inferable from position relative to aria-current, which mitigates the default case, but status overrides and the replaced step number are not conveyed: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1 (and 1.1.1 for the CSS tick conveying state). docs/dga-reference.md:77 asks for `a text equivalent` of progress; docs/stepper-states.md:123-124 relies on `numbers/check marks and aria-current`, which covers colour-only (1.4.1) but not programmatic state.

subject: menu
title: Menu type-ahead exists only in vanilla
description: Vanilla createMenu moves focus to the next enabled item whose label starts with the typed characters (500 ms buffer). React, Vue and Angular menus ignore printable keys: their menu keydown handlers only handle ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End/Escape/Tab. The guide summary advertises type-ahead for Menu without restriction.

evidence.quote: Presents a compact list of actions with roving keyboard focus, disabled-item skipping, and typeahead.

expected: Same type-ahead in every adapter, as vanilla does and as WAI-ARIA APG Menu Button / Menu pattern keyboard interaction describes (printable character moves to the next item starting with it).
fix: Move the type-ahead search into a core helper (vanilla already uses normalizeSearch) and call it from the React, Vue and Angular menu keydown handlers.

subject: menu
title: Menu API differs in item shape, events, trigger, open control and markup across adapters
description: React: items {value,label:ReactNode,disabled,href,onSelect}, any trigger element, open/defaultOpen/onOpenChange, onAction(value), no disabled prop. Vue: items {value,label:string,disabled,href}, built-in trigger whose text is the same `label` that names the menu (or a trigger slot), disabled, emits select(value), no open/update:open (open state is internal). Angular: items {id,label,disabled} (id instead of value, no href items), text-only trigger `triggerLabel` defaulting to English 'Open' (no icon-only trigger, no trigger aria-label), [(open)] inherited from HwPopoverComponent, output action(id). Vanilla: authored markup, data-hw-value, onSelect, hw:change {value}. Rendered menu structure also differs: React/Vue ul.hw-menu-list > li[role=none] > button/a; Angular div.hw-menu-panel > button.hw-menu-item.

evidence.quote: export interface MenuProps extends Omit<ComponentPropsWithRef<'div'>, 'onSelect'> { items: readonly MenuItem[]; label: string; trigger: ReactElement<ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>>; open?: boolean; defaultOpen?: boolean; onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void; onAction?: (value: string) => void }
export interface HwMenuItem { id: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean; }

expected: One documented Menu contract in all adapters (CONTRACT.md and AGENTS.md: keep behavior, APIs and examples synchronized): same item identifier name, same selection event payload, controlled and uncontrolled open in every framework, link items everywhere, a customizable trigger (including icon-only with an accessible name) and no English-only defaults.
fix: Align on one item shape ({value,label,disabled,href}) and one event name/payload; add open/defaultOpen/update:open to Vue, href items and trigger content projection to Angular, a disabled prop to React; replace the 'Open' default with a required label.

subject: popover
title: Popover closes when focus leaves only in vanilla
description: Vanilla createPopover closes the panel on focusout to an element outside the root. React, Vue and Angular listen only for outside pointerdown and Escape, so tabbing past the panel leaves it open over later content. The guide states focus leaving closes the panel.

evidence.quote: scope.listen(root, 'focusout', event => { const next = (event as FocusEvent).relatedTarget as Node | null; if (next && !root.contains(next)) close(); });
const outside = (event: PointerEvent) => { if (!root.current?.contains(event.target as Node)) setOpen(false); };
Outside press or focus leaving closes the panel without trapping focus.

fix: Add a focusout handler (relatedTarget outside root => close without focus restore) to the React, Vue and Angular popovers.

subject: popover
title: React Popover closes on Escape pressed anywhere in the document and moves focus to its trigger
description: The React escape listener is registered on the document and does not check where focus is. With a popover open and focus on an unrelated control elsewhere, Escape closes the popover and focuses its trigger, pulling focus away from where the user is. Vue checks the root keydown, Angular checks host.contains(event.target), vanilla listens on its root.

evidence.quote: const escape = (event: KeyboardEvent) => { if (event.key === 'Escape' && !event.defaultPrevented) { event.preventDefault(); setOpen(false); opener.current?.focus(); } };

expected: Escape handled only when focus is inside the popover (Angular interactions.ts:31, vanilla disclosures.ts:24); focus is never moved from an unrelated element.
fix: Attach the keydown handler to the root element or check root.contains(event.target) before closing/focusing.
repro: <scratch>/audit/work/nav-b/t-popover2.cjs: open popover, focus #after button outside it, press Escape. <scratch>/audit/work/nav-b/out-popover2.txt: react 'escFocusOutsideWhileOpen=exp=false/H f=TRIG'; vanilla/vue/angular keep focus on 'after'.
verifierNote: Read react/src/expanded-interactive.tsx:29-30 (keydown listener on ownerDocument, no target check); compared vue :183-189 (root onKeydown), angular :31 (host.contains(event.target)), vanilla disclosures.ts:24 (root keydown). Ran <scratch>/audit/verify/nav-b/behave.cjs (output <scratch>/audit/verify/nav-b/out-behave-1.txt, <scratch>/audit/verify/nav-b/out-behave-2.txt): open popover, focus #after outside it, press Escape. Moving focus away from where the user is on an unrelated key press is a focus-order/unexpected change problem (WCAG 2.4.3 / 3.2.1 context).

subject: popover
title: Popover naming, heading and trigger API differ; the same example renders a heading only in React and vanilla
description: React requires title (rendered as an <h3> and used via aria-labelledby) and a trigger element; it has no disabled prop.
